a.v: Attest is a documented approval of a purchase. Every purchase made on the guild's behalf must be attested, and attest is given once the purchase has been reported.

v: A result owner may attest every purchase made under their result unit.

a.v: Nobody may attest their own purchases. The app never shows your own expense in your approval queue.

Which result unit a purchase belongs to is decided by the cost center it is reported on. If a purchase is split across cost centers under several result units, each part is attested by its own result owner.

items.q: Which result units are there, and who is the result owner?

a.v: A cost center's code starts with its result unit's prefix, so SEX01 belongs to Sexmästeriet and is attested by Sexmästaren.

items.q: What should I check before I approve?

a.v: The documentation has to be satisfactory. Ask yourself these questions before approving the purchase:

v: Is it a valid receipt, in the state the seller gave it?
Does the date given match the date on the receipt?
Is the description appropriate for the goods?
Is there budget for the purchase on the cost center, or a budget change that covers it?
Is guild card or out-of-pocket correctly chosen?
For mileage: is the route filled in, and does the distance match it? A round trip should have the starting point both first and last.

a.v: You attest per cost center. If the purchase is split across several, you only approve the rows you answer for, and the rest wait for whoever answers for them.

items.q: What happens if a purchase is not attested?

a.v: Then it is paid for by whoever made the purchase. An out-of-pocket expense is not reimbursed, and a guild card purchase is invoiced to the person who made it.
The treasurer can, given the circumstances of the individual case, decide that reimbursement is paid anyway or that no invoice is sent.
